blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the heal ledger's estimate charges do not accumulate unboundedly across sweeps (per-sweep ledger, run-id dedup, or a reset) so the budget cap is not permanently tripped.
evidence: heal.py:203-204: `result = attempter.run(criterion_id)` then unconditional `_record_spend(criterion_id, tier, sample_n, result.usage_rows, ledger_file)`
heal.py:257-263 `charge_estimate` is always called when usage_rows is empty; `_record_spend` run_id is `heal-{criterion_prompt_id(criterion_id)}` (heal.py:242) with no dedup against prior sweeps
ledger.py:82-83 `_spent_so_far` sums ALL rows across the append-only file; the CLI uses a persistent path `.rebar/fixture_heal_ledger.jsonl` (_llm_eval_commands.py:132) reused across sweeps
fixture_admission.py:158-160 admission dedups its own `admission-{prompt_id}` run_id, but heal's estimate charge has no equivalent guard, so each sweep re-charges the estimate for the same criteria
heal.py:465-475 `_run_admission` passes `ledger_path=ledger_path` so `run_admission` writes to the SAME ledger
fixture_admission.py:224-232 admission calls `ledger.finalize(f"admission-{prompt_id}", ...)` on admit
heal.py:462 the production solver returns `CaseOutcome(fired=..., usage_rows=[])` — always empty
heal.py:203-204 heal then unconditionally calls `_record_spend`, adding a second ledger entry per attempt
blocking.finding: The heal loop's spend ledger accumulates a charge_estimate row on every sweep with no idempotency guard and no reset, so cumulative `spent` grows without bound across the scheduled (default 30-day) sweeps and will eventually exceed cap_usd permanently, causing every future sweep to stop for budget on the first criterion.
merged_from: For an ADMITTED criterion, both `run_admission` (via its own `ledger.finalize`) and the heal loop's `_record_spend` write ledger entries for the same attempt, double-counting spend; the module docstring claims admission `finalize` 'records actual cost' but the production solver returns empty `usage_rows`, so admission records $0 and only the estimate is charged — a mismatch between the documented contract and actual behaviour.
scenarios: A repo runs `rebar criteria heal` on the scheduled interval for several months; the persistent ledger keeps growing and eventually `spent >= 25.0`, after which no criterion is ever attempted again.
A criterion already admitted in a prior sweep is re-charged an estimate on each subsequent sweep.
